title_html: AI tools that work on school networks in China
lede: Chinese AI services that teachers and students can usually reach without extra setup, grouped by job. All of them are Chinese-run services on Chinese domains. Access varies by school network, so test each one before class.

tools.name: Kimi
tools.good_for: Research, writing, slides, and simple websites. Log in with WeChat or Google.

tools.name: DeepSeek
tools.good_for: Reasoning, math, writing, and coding help

tools.name: Doubao
tools.good_for: Everyday questions, writing, and voice chat

tools.name: Yuanbao
tools.good_for: Questions, writing, and search with sources

tools.name: Zhipu Qingyan
tools.good_for: Writing and study help, with a learning mode

tools.name: TRAE
tools.good_for: AI coding editor: describe it, then build it

blocked.h: Usually not available without extra setup
blocked.p: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini (personal accounts), Perplexity, Midjourney, and Cursor do not officially serve mainland China. Websites published on vercel.app addresses are often blocked as well, so publish student work to an address your school can open.

licensed.p: Microsoft 365 Copilot is not available on the China version of Microsoft 365 (operated by 21Vianet). Schools on a global Microsoft 365 setup should check their own license with IT.

items: Test each tool on the student network, not only the staff network.
Keep a backup: a phone hotspot, or a second tool that does the same job.
Use placeholder data. No real student names or records in any tool.
Agree on accounts and logins with your IT team before students sign up.
Most of these services say they are mainly for adults and require guardian consent for users under 18; several add extra steps for under-14s.
China's Personal Information Protection Law treats under-14s' personal information as sensitive and requires guardian consent (Articles 28 and 31).
Vidu is 18+ only and is left off this list. Claude requires users to be 18+; ChatGPT requires 13+ with parent permission under 18.

footer_left: Checked October 15, 2026, from each tool’s official site and terms. Access and names change often; confirm with your IT team.
